name: Borderlands 4: Kairos
description: Walk a slice of Borderlands 4's open world, baked offline by bl4x, with Quake 3 player kinematics

unit_scale.explanation: bl4x's placement walker already writes metres (UE centimetres / 100), so nothing is rescaled.

axis_convention.source: Unreal Engine: Z-up, x forward, y right, centimetres, quaternion xyzw
axis_convention.engine: Y-up, x east-ish, z south-ish, metres, quaternion xyzw
axis_convention.mapping: glTF convention (Y up), the same one bl4x's walker already emits -- see D:\BL4Export\src\cpp\world\walker.hpp.
axis_convention.critical: Applied once, inside bl4x itself (world/walker.cpp). The engine only ever reads already-converted placements.json/world.json; nothing downstream re-maps axes.

world_bounds_metres.note: Unbounded, same idea as packages/fs2024: bl4.tiles.resolve/load/evict stream a grid of tiles keyed by floor(x / tile_size), floor(z / tile_size) around the player. Only tiles bl4x actually baked exist; the grid itself is a baking convention (see README.md), not something BL4's own World Partition cells expose.

player.explanation: The ioq3 pmove chain (q3.pm.*) unchanged, borrowing gta5's walking tune. Its traces sweep whichever archetype's btBvhTriangleMeshShape the player is currently over -- see bl4_collision_shape.cpp.

asset_pipeline.reason: BL4's IoStore archives are read by a separate, standalone tool (bl4x, outside this repo) that decodes Zen packages, Nanite mesh clusters, and Virtual Textures from scratch. This package only ever reads bl4x's already-baked output.
asset_pipeline.expected_input: <BL4_MAP_DIR>/world.json plus <BL4_MAP_DIR>/tiles/<tx>_<tz>/placements.json and <BL4_MAP_DIR>/models/*.obj, written by `bl4x bake <out_dir> <tile_size> <cell1.umap> [cell2.umap ...]`. See README.md.

notes: Borrows gta5.sky.draw with the gta5 sky/composite shaders, gta5.gamepad, gta5.player.fly, and quake3's input aggregation config. Meshes currently draw with one placeholder texture (bl4x doesn't resolve UMaterialInstance -> texture parameters yet), so this is a geometry-and-movement slice, not a textured one.
